At Innsworth Schools’ Partnership, we believe that music, in its many forms, is a vital part of our cultures and therefore studying music allows us an additional window into learning about the world, it peoples, and its history, as well as being a tool for self-expression and an important subject in its own right.
Singing, in particular group singing, can be instrumental in fostering a sense of belonging and has been shown to improve mental health and this is why we have chosen an approach which puts singing at the heart of our provision.
The children learn about music by listening to, singing and playing music from different cultures and time periods. Through this, they develop their knowledge of the inter-related dimensions of music (pitch, duration, dynamics, tempo, timbre, texture, structure and appropriate musical notations). As they move through the schools, children become more adept at discussing music and using their ideas and musical knowledge to compose short pieces and songs.
In addition to the main music curriculum, there are other opportunities for children to engage in music making across the partnership, for example: school productions, concerts, clubs and individual music lessons.

Governing Body – Innsworth Schools’ Partnership
The majority of children from Innsworth Infant School transfer to Innsworth Junior School to complete their primary phase education. Each school had its own Governing Body. While the two schools had always worked together, in 2013 it was agreed that even closer cooperation could be achieved, resulting in a better educational ‘offering’ to pupils, by federating the two governing bodies into one. This occurred on September 1, 2014 and the Innsworth Schools’ Partnership came into being. The ties between the schools were further strengthened by the appointment of Mrs Lisa Jones as Executive Headteacher on September 1, 2015, with responsibility for both schools.
The overall role of Governors is to support the Headteacher and the staff – the phrase often used to describe this role is ‘a critical friend’. Governors help the Headteacher and Staff to set and reach targets and to strive for excellence across the whole spectrum of school life. The two key documents used for this are the Partnership Development Plan (PDP) and the Self Evaluation Form (SEF). The PDP sets out a strategic plan for the school, with targets that everyone works towards and the SEF sets out how well the school is doing and where we aim to make improvements.
Statutory duties of the Governing Body include:-
The Governing Body meets at least once every term (6 meetings per academic year). Committees look at particular areas of school life under the headings, Learning, Resourcing and Staffing. All governors are informed about what happens at these meetings.
Learning Committee - looks at pupil progress and attainment, and the quality and consistency of teaching.Resourcing and Staffing Committee – looks at how the school budgets are being spent, within the classroom, and on buildings and facilities. Looks at all aspects of school life affecting and affected by staff.
There are several categories of governor, representing different groups that have an interest in the schools. These are the Headteacher, Parent Governors (elected by parents) and a Staff Governor (elected by staff from both schools). This group of Governors convened the first meeting of the FGB and then co-opted further governors to complete the FGB. One of those co-opted governors is nominated by the local authority, Gloucestershire County Council. Co-opted governors are appointed because of their specific expertise or the experience which they can bring to the FGB.
The children at both schools are at the heart of everything the Headteacher, Staff and Governors do. We are committed to providing an environment, where all aspects, physical, emotional, academic and playful, can be enjoyed by all of our children so that by the end of the primary stage of their education, they have all had the opportunity to ‘enjoy, achieve, aspire’. This is the inspiration behind the establishment of the Innsworth Schools’ Partnership.

At Innsworth Schools’ Partnership, we believe that art provides all children with an alternative means of expressing and sharing their ideas, thoughts and feelings. We encourage children to see themselves as artists and to become comfortable with their creativity, in whatever form it may take.
The children take inspiration from a range of artists, both living and historical, from a range of cultures which reflect the diversity of our school community. We aim to develop understanding of fundamental visual concepts in art and design (line, colour, texture, pattern, shape and 3D form) by talking about, and evaluating critically, the work of different artists. We then move to a more practical approach which focuses on drawing skills and experimenting with, and developing control of, a range of media.
Children use sketchbooks from Reception all the way up to Year 6. We encourage the children to think of their sketchbooks as a place where they can record their thoughts, feelings and ideas (both written and visual) as well as where they can experiment with different ideas or media and practice different techniques.

At Innsworth Schools’ Partnership we believe that Design and Technology is crucial in allowing children to develop practical skills for a sustainable future. Our curriculum provides a framework in which children are able to develop their cooking, sewing and engineering skills over time and think critically about design and how good design can improve the world around them.
Our aim is for our children to be confident in talking about, preparing and cooking simple dishes from around the world, reflecting the multi-national character of our school community. We also teach basic sewing techniques so that they will have the skills to be able to mend, recycle and embellish clothes and other fabric articles in the future. In our engineering curriculum, we encourage the children to experiment with a range of mechanisms, materials and components and carry out practical tasks with increasing accuracy through selecting and using a wider range of tools and equipment as they progress through the schools.
Design Technology has the added benefit of allowing children to develop resourcefulness, resilience and problem solving skills. Children are also able to apply skills learned in other disciplines (such as maths, science and art) in a practical way and are encouraged to work constructively with others to analyse and evaluate, make mistakes, share them and learn from them.

Humanities at Innsworth Infant School
At Innsworth Infant School Humanities provides children with the opportunity to develop a curiosity and fascination about the world, its people and the past.
Throughout their explorations in Topic, and as part of their Geography learning, children will study places and the relationships between people and their environments. They will be inspired to link their learning to real life experiences, building connections between themselves, our local area and the wider world community. Our Geography curriculum provides opportunities to explore the world using maps, globes, atlases, images and videos which promotes the application of Geographical skills. Pupils are taught to identify human and physical features comparing their local area and other places. This allows us to build on our connections we have with a wide range of communities and deepen their understanding of places around the world.
The teaching of History promotes an enquiry approach encouraging the children to ask and answer questions building on what they already know and what they could find out. It provides them with the opportunity to study people and events in the past, in particular noticing the changes, making comparisons and reflecting on their effect over time. Pupils are taught to investigate by making observations and inferences about the past and use a wide range of sources including images and artefacts as evidence. Our History curriculum encourages them to discuss their findings, justify their opinions as well as value others opinions. It is important to us that History is made accessible to the children and that connections are made where they can connect their findings to their own, real life experiences.

Maths
We follow a mastery approach to the teaching and learning of Mathematics in our school. We believe that all children should work together to become fluent mathematicians who are able to reason and solve a variety of problems by applying what they have learned in a range of contexts.
We use the Can Do Maths resources to support our curriculum provision in EYFS, Y1 and Y2 alongside resources from NCETM, I See Maths and White Rose Maths. Our curriculum promotes a deep, long-term, secure and adaptable understanding of the subject so that children are fluent at mathematics. We expect children to reason mathematically and develop the ability to apply maths to solve problems. Children’s conceptual understanding is developed through concrete and visual representations and children are given opportunities to explain their reasoning as part of our daily maths lessons. Our teaching focuses on developing a secure and deep understanding, using practical resources alongside formal representations which supports the learning and memorisation of mathematical concepts.
We are participating in the Mastering Number Programme which creates secure firm foundations in the development of good number sense for all children from Reception through to Year 1 and Year 2. The aim, over time, is that children will leave KS1 with fluency in calculation and a confidence and flexibility with number. Attention is given to key knowledge and understanding needed in Reception classes, and progression through KS1 to support success in the future.
In the Early Years, early mathematical understanding is achieved during both child initiated play and adult teaching through meaningful contexts, so that all children have daily moments where they explicitly engage with mathematical concepts and language. Emphasis is given to developing children’s spatial reasoning. Spatial reasoning involves our interpretation of how things, including ourselves, relate to each other and our spatial environment. In education and in everyday life, we use spatial reasoning to interpret images, create representations and in (mental) manipulation, enabling us to predict and solve problems.

PE at Innsworth Infant School
We believe that all students deserve the opportunity to participate in physical activity that is fun and contributes to a healthy balanced lifestyle.
Our approach is focused on allowing children to develop key skills such as movement and spatial awareness, through a carefully planned curriculum focusing on skills instead of specific sports. We allow children to then improve these key skills through a variety of games and skill-based practices.
Our curriculum is based on six different themes that are progressive from EYFS to Year 2 to allow children to extend and develop their skillset. As children complete Year 2 they should be able to confidently participate in games using their previously learnt skills to support teamwork and positive outcomes.
We celebrate success in PE at our school through athletes of the term, the focus is on their participation and engagement in the intended learning.
